entry.title: Where to find Cooling Fans in ARC Raiders
entry.summary:
Loot is a core part of ARC Raiders, with all sorts of items and pieces of loot necessary to progress in the game, whether it be upgrading workstations, advancing the Expedition projects, or crafting the best equipment and weapons.
Cooling Fans were required for one of the Expedition projects, and will probably be necessary to advance other events and projects down the line, making them a good item to stock up on just in case.
Here's where you can find them.
How to get Cooling Fans in ARC Raiders
The Launch Towers are a generally fantastic loot spot, but also a great source of Cooling Fans. Screenshot and remix by Destructoid
Cooling Fans can be found in Technological loot zones, which are located on just about every map in the game. However, we've had the most luck with them when raiding the Launch Towers on the Spaceport map, specifically the very top parts.
All the containers and tables are chock full of every kind of item you can think of, including Cooling Fans, which tend to spawn quite often (you'll usually get at least one per run, unless your luck is really bad that day).
On the other hand, this item can spawn within Server Racks, breachable containers that spawn on a lot of the maps, but are most easily accessed on Dam Battlegrounds. They can only be opened if you have the relevant perk unlocked in the Survival tree, which I suggest you get not only for the Cooling Fans, but for a lot of additional great loot that spawns within them as well.
Cooling Fans are, as said above, necessary for the Expeditions, so you'd do well to have a few lying in your inventory just in case they're required for any further events.

entry.title: Where to find Synthesized Fuel in ARC Raiders
entry.summary:
ARC Raiders is chock full of various items that you must find by any means necessary to progress. Many of the game's quests, alongside much of its secondary progressions, are tied to unique items that can be either looted, crafted, purchased, or recycled from other pieces of loot.
Synthesized Fuel is one such item, though it's a lot easier to obtain than most other loot we've covered so far.
If you're having trouble finding it, here's what you should do.
How to get Synthesized Fuel in ARC Raiders
The Assembly is a great place to look for Exodus items like the Rocket Thrusters that'll provide two Synthesized Fuels when recycled. Screenshot and remix by Destructoid
The absolutely easiest way to obtain Synthesized Fuel is to purchase it from Celeste. She sells it from time to time for a few Assorted Seeds a pop, meaning you'll have to stock up on these through topside runs, looting them straight or recycling Herbs that you find across the game's maps.
On the other hand, Synthesized Fuel can be looted or recycled, with the latter being the more productive way. On Spaceport and Stella Montis, you can find Rocket Thrusters in Exodus loot areas, with each providing you with a couple of Synthesized Fuels per recycle. The item doesn't have that much use outside of being recycled or sold, so it's a very productive source of Synthesized Fuel, which will put your mind at ease.
It's almost guaranteed to appear in the Assembly on Stella Montis or other Exodus areas in the game, so you should check them out if Celeste purchases aren't an option.

entry.title: How to get and use Cobalt in Hytale
entry.summary:
Cobalt is one of the several metals you can find in Hytale, and it will be your source for getting some wonderful armor pieces.
The metal is necessary for crafting various gear pieces, and it's less common than Copper or Iron. Once found, you'll also need to convert it into ingots. You can then use them in recipes, depending on what you have unlocked.
Let's look at how to get Cobalt in Hytale, and what its best uses are.
Table of contents Best location for finding Cobalt in Hytale How to use Cobalt in Hytale
Best location for finding Cobalt in Hytale
To find this rare item, you'll want to head to the Whisperfront Frontiers biome. This snowy area has plenty of Shale columns located around the biome. You can mine them to get Cobalt. Typically, the amount of resources you get will be low due to their rarity. Once you find a deposit, extract as much as you can.
Screenshot by Destructoid
You can also find Cobalt in the same biome, but below the ground. The quantity you'll get is significantly lower, so it's not my favorite choice.
How to use Cobalt in Hytale
The raw Cobalt you get can't be used as a standalone item. The first thing you'll require is a Furnace. You can make a Furnace at your base, which will then allow you to smelt metals (including Cobalt). When you add fuel and Cobalt to your Furnace, you'll get Cobalt Ingots in return.
Here's a list of recipes I have found so far that require Cobalt Ingot.
Cobalt Sword
Cobalt Helm
Cobalt Cuirass
Cobalt Gauntlets
Cobalt Greaves
Cobalt Shield
You will also require a bunch of Cobalt Ingots to upgrade the Furnace, which allows you to do better smelting (and add efficiency).
If you've already found the necessary items but are unsure how to use them, here's a list of all craftable weapons and armors in the current build.

entry.title: USN-7963-1: libpng vulnerabilities
entry.summary:
It was discovered that the libpng simplified API incorrectly processed palette PNG images with partial transparency and gamma correction. If a user or automated system were tricked into opening a specially crafted PNG file, an attacker could use this issue to cause libpng to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2025-66293)
Petr Simecek, Stanislav Fort and Pavel Kohout discovered that the libpng simplified API incorrectly processed interlaced 16-bit PNGs with 8-bit output format and non-minimal row strides. If a user or automated system were tricked into opening a specially crafted PNG file, an attacker could use this issue to cause libpng to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2026-22695)
Cosmin Truta discovered that the libpng simplified API incorrectly handled invalid row strides. If a user or automated system were tricked into opening a specially crafted PNG file, an attacker could use this issue to cause libpng to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2026-22801)

entry.title: FC 26 maintenance (Jan. 14): When will the servers be back
entry.summary:
EA Sports has announced a new maintenance for FC 26 that will take place today across all platforms, and it will heavily impact online connectivity.
This is the first major maintenance in the new year, and it comes ahead of the TOTY celebrations. Thankfully, EA Sports has announced the complete schedule that will allow you to keep track of when the servers will be down.
FC 26 server maintenance details (Jan. 14)
The servers will go down before the maintenance actually begins. Today's maintenance starts 11pm ET/1am CT/2am ET/7am UTC across all platforms. Older titles like FC 25 will also be down when the maintenance is live. Matchmaking will go down 30 minutes before the actual maintenance begins.
The maintenance is scheduled to last for five hours. Unless there are delays, the maintenance should be over by 4am ET/6am CT/7am ET/12am UTC. That said, there can always be delays during maintenance. If that happens, I will duly add the updated timings to this guide.
Once the matchmaking is disabled, all forms of online games will be out of order. Modes like Ultimate Team will also become inaccessible. You should still be able to enjoy content on the Web app and Companion app. However, logging in via your PC/console should be disabled. Even if you manage to get in, trying to start a fresh match will result in an error.
It will be interesting to find out if EA Sports will be making any live tuning upgrades during the maintenance. The last major patch, Title Update 1.4.0, came out earlier in January, and it made some heavy changes to AI-defending and movement.
Of course, this maintenance might be in preparation for the upcoming TOTY promo. We already have confirmed dates about when the promo begins and which players are going to feature on the starting lineups.

entry.title: How to complete Hi, Doggy in Quarantine Zone: The Last Check and feed the zombie
entry.summary:
The Hi, Doggy quest not only has a funny name, but it's a rather interesting task to complete in Quarantine Zone: The Last Check.
The Hi, Doggy is a relatively early game quest that you can unlock on day 10. It's a core campaign quest, so there's no way of skipping it (unless you're playing in the Endless mode). This guide will help you figure out how to feed your zombie.
Table of contents How to start Hi, Doggy quest in Quarantine Zone: The Last Check How to feed the zombie in Hi, Doggy quest
How to start Hi, Doggy quest in Quarantine Zone: The Last Check
The quest begins at the start of day 10 when the major briefs you about what needs to be done. When you're in the early game, there's not much you can do with a zombie in Quarantine. However, this quest will introduce you to the Cage in the Laboratory.
Image via Devolver Digital
The Cage can contain an undead and allow you to study for research. You'll find the Cage to the right of the main lab tent (from where you can discover new symptoms). Your next task is to feed the zombie. Head straight from the lab gates, and you'll end up in front of the locked zombie.
How to feed the zombie in Hi, Doggy quest
Image via Devolver Digital
This task is pretty simple. Go to the Liquidation zone, where you send the infected to be chopped. You'll find a marked area by the pile of bags. Pick up a body bag, put it on the card, and go back to the laboratory tent. If you can't pick up the body, chances are that the cart isn't close enough. Interact with the cart and bring it closer to the body bags.
Image via Devolver Digital
Park the cart next to the Cage, and interact with the body bag carrying the corpse. Pick it up, and put it in the Cage, and the zombie will start to eat. This will complete the Hi, Doggy quest. Make sure to put the cart in the highlighted zone so that the corpse can be fed to the zombie trapped inside.

Being opt-in, Expeditions are designed to be a gentler alternative to the playerbase-wide seasonal ‘prestiging’ mechanics or progression wipes of other online games. Developers Embark say just over a million people took part in the first Expedition – Arc Raiders has sold around 12 million copies to date – with "something close to about 35% or 40%” of those players bagging the full set of Expedition skill points, in the words of design director Virgil Watkins.

entry.title: OpenTTD 15.0-RC4
entry.summary: Third, er, Fourth try’s the charm? You found some bugs that needed fixing before the full release of OpenTTD 15. Let’s do one last (we hope) Release Candidate. As always, if you spot any more bugs, please report them here. We’ve heard from many of our translators that they’ve finished their languages. If your language needs updating, it’s the last chance! entry.title: French Torrent Giant YggTorrent Faces User Revolt after Introducing Paid ‘Turbo Mode’
entry.summary: YggTorrent, the largest francophone torrent community, faces widespread pushback after it introduced a paid 'Turbo Mode' for €86 this week. For regular users, the tracker now has a limit of five torrent downloads per day and a 30-second download delay. According to the site's operators, these restrictions are needed to deter bots and ban hit-and-run downloads. From: TF, for the latest news on copyright battles, piracy and more.

entry.title: Anna’s Archive Backed Up Spotify, Plans to Release 300TB Music Archive
entry.summary: In what appears to be the largest music leak in history, Anna’s Archive says it has made a multi-terabyte 'backup' of Spotify, including metadata for nearly the entire catalog and audio files for 86 million tracks. While Anna's Archive typically focuses on books and other texts, it says the opportunity to help preserve 'humanity's musical heritage' couldn't be ignored. From: TF, for the latest news on copyright battles, piracy and more.
